example.title: Protect a bearer-only employee API
description: Each example is a separate project. All required application files appear in the tabs.
The environment supplies `JWT_ISSUER_URI` and `JWT_AUDIENCE` from a trusted authorization-server setup.
The authorization server issues an `RS256`-signed JWT access token for that audience with the scope `employee.read`.
This API accepts bearer credentials only through the `Authorization` header. It does not support session-cookie, form-login, or HTTP Basic authentication.
Requests use HTTPS outside local development.
explanation: The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <access-token>` with its API request.
The decoder checks signature, issuer, timestamps, and the configured audience.
The scope becomes `SCOPE_employee.read`, which satisfies the GET permission rule.
Other methods and paths are denied.
`STATELESS` prevents Spring Security from using a session to obtain authentication.
CSRF is disabled only because this configuration has no automatically attached browser credentials.
A missing or invalid token normally produces `401`.
A valid token without the required scope produces `403`.
Password-account ownership can use local usernames. A JWT API must first map the trusted issuer and subject to its local account before applying that ownership rule.

files.code:
spring:
  security:
    oauth2:
      resourceserver:
        jwt:
          issuer-uri: ${JWT_ISSUER_URI}
          audiences:
            - ${JWT_AUDIENCE}
